Task 1 execution record (141.001-T) — DIAGNOSIS ONLY, no source/test file changed.

STEP 1 (baseline, canonical gate): $env:PYTHONPATH=src; python -m unittest discover -s tests.
Ran 1718 tests, FAILED (failures=3, errors=2, skipped=20). Exact 5 IDs reproduced,
identical to the E8158860 baseline:
- ERROR test_repo_root_artifacts.RepoRootTrackedJsonAllowlistTest.test_root_tracked_json_matches_allowlist
- ERROR test_telemetry_gitignore_template.MetricsEmissionHardGateTests.test_emitted_metrics_artifacts_are_never_tracked
- FAIL  test_gate_pipeline_topology_cli.PipelineTopologyStorageRootResolutionTests.test_backlog_only_workspace_succeeds
- FAIL  test_gates_topology.FilesystemTopologyReadersTests.test_empty_queue_and_archive_dirs_pass_as_zero_shipments
- FAIL  test_telemetry_gitignore_template.MetricsGitignoreTests.test_git_check_ignore_matches_metrics_artifacts

AC2 (git init exit-128 stderr, VERBATIM, binding in both verdicts): the default
unittest traceback for these CalledProcessError instances does NOT print
.stderr (Python CalledProcessError string form omits it), so it had never
actually been captured despite the failure being known. Captured it via a
non-committed diagnostic wrapper (monkeypatching subprocess.run to print
stdout/stderr on CalledProcessError, run once, discarded -- no source or
test file was modified) around the SAME canonical discover invocation:

  cmd: git.EXE ls-files -z -- *.json
  returncode: 128
  stdout: (empty)
  stderr: error: missing config value GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2 / fatal: unable to parse command-line config

  cmd: git init
  returncode: 128
  stdout: (empty)
  stderr: error: missing config value GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2 / fatal: unable to parse command-line config

Both failing git invocations produce the IDENTICAL stderr. This is git's
environment-variable command-line-config-injection mechanism
(GIT_CONFIG_COUNT / GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n / GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n): git requires
every declared GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n (n less than GIT_CONFIG_COUNT) to have a matching
GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n present in the environment, or it fails ALL git
invocations in that process with exactly this message.

STEP 2 (confirm the exclusion result, amendment A5 -- MANDATORY protocol
step): ran the deterministic positive dotted-name enumeration of the
complement set (84 of 87 tests/test_*.py modules, i.e. every module except
the three test_scope_containment_* modules the 024-DL entry hypothesized as
the polluter). Result: Ran 1616 tests, FAILED (failures=3, errors=2,
skipped=20) -- the EXACT SAME 5 failure/error IDs listed above, byte-identical,
reproduced WITHOUT the three test_scope_containment_* modules present at all.

Expected green; actual NOT green. Per the FIXED protocol ("If NOT green,
the entry premise is falsified, record VERDICT INCONCLUSIVE with the
falsification evidence and STOP"), the entry own established fact
("all five pass when the three test_scope_containment_* modules are absent")
is FALSIFIED. STOPPING here per the mandatory protocol step 2 gate -- no
bisection rounds were run, because the premise the bisection would have
narrowed from is itself false.

SUPPLEMENTARY DIAGNOSTIC COLOR (not part of the required bisection, gathered
because it materially explains the falsification and is safe, read-only
evidence-gathering -- no test subsets were run to narrow a polluter/victim
pair, so this does not contradict the STOP):
- Literal-text search (grep, no bisection) for GIT_CONFIG_COUNT /
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY / GIT_CONFIG_VALUE across every .py file under tests/
  and src/autoharness/: ZERO matches. Also searched every .py file under
  .venv/Lib/site-packages/ (installed third-party dependencies): ZERO
  matches. No code in this repository or its dependencies sets, reads, or
  reacts to these environment variables anywhere.
- A fresh shell in this same execution environment already carries
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.bareRepository /
  VALUE_0=explicit, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=credential.interactive /
  VALUE_1=never, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2=core.fsmonitor / VALUE_2= (present as
  an empty string at the PowerShell/.NET layer). A plain git status / git
  version invocation in that same fresh shell succeeds despite the empty
  VALUE_2 -- but the SAME triple, inherited by a long-running python -m
  unittest discover process os.environ and passed through unmodified to
  a child subprocess.run(git ...) call partway through the suite,
  produces "missing config value GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2" (not merely empty --
  ABSENT). This is consistent with the well-documented Windows behavior that
  SetEnvironmentVariable(name, empty string) DELETES the
  variable from the true Win32 process environment block rather than storing
  an empty value, while a shell-level .NET view can still display it
  as present-but-blank via a cached/different code path. Given zero code
  references anywhere in this repository or its dependencies, the deletion
  mechanism (if this theory is correct) is NOT triggered by any file this
  task is permitted to change, and is either (a) an ambient host/sandbox
  environment characteristic external to this codebase entirely, or (b) a
  Python-runtime/OS-level interaction not visible to a source-level grep.
  This is offered as color for the successor shipment own investigation,
  not as a finding this task is scoped to resolve or fix.

NARROWED CANDIDATE SET (AC4): the polluter is NOT confined to the three
test_scope_containment_* modules -- that hypothesis is falsified. The
remaining candidate space is the other 84 tests/test_*.py modules (unnarrowed
further, since no bisection rounds were run per the STOP instruction), OR the
root cause is not test-code-order-dependent at all but an ambient
environment/OS-level condition unrelated to which tests execute (a
possibility the supplementary diagnostic color above supports but does not
prove). Rounds performed: 0 (stopped at the mandatory step-2 gate before any
bisection round began, per the FIXED protocol -- no fourth attempt, no
speculative fix).

Scope guard (024-DL R5): this diagnosis does NOT implicate any file under
src/autoharness/ -- the grep above found zero references to the
GIT_CONFIG_* mechanism anywhere in this repository own source, so no
re-capture into P-021 is triggered by this finding.

Canonical unittest suite (baseline, for the task record): Ran 1718 tests,
5 failures/errors -- identical to the known pre-existing E8158860 signature,
confirmed by this task own step 1. No new failures introduced (no
source/test file changed by this task).

VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE

AC1-AC5 disposition: AC1 (PAIR-ISOLATED only) N/A. AC2 satisfied (verbatim
git stderr captured above, both failing invocations). AC3 (PAIR-ISOLATED
only) N/A. AC4 satisfied (narrowed candidate set + supplementary diagnostic
color recorded above, consumable by 151-S own Step 0 gate). AC5 satisfied
(exactly one VERDICT token: INCONCLUSIVE).
